sentences.text: On January 9, 2026, Austin EMS documented a 41-year-old male restrained driver who was rear-ended at approx. 35 mph, complained of neck pain 7/10 and headache, was alert and oriented, and was transported to Central ER.

On January 9, 2026, the Central ER discharge summary documented a diagnosis of cervical strain and concussion without loss of consciousness, a negative CT head, a prescription for cyclobenzaprine 10 mg, and follow up with PCP in 1 week.
On January 16, 2026, Dr. Alvarez documented persistent neck pain 6/10 and daily headaches and referred the patient to physical therapy 2x/week for 6 weeks.
On January 23, 2026, Capital PT's initial evaluation documented cervical range of motion reduced approx. 40% and a plan of care of 12 visits.
On February 20, 2026, Capital PT documented at visit 8 pain of 4/10, improving, and that the patient reports missing 3 days of work.
On May 18, 2026, Hill Country Pain Management documented new onset pain radiating to right arm with numbness in fingers, pain 7/10, and that an MRI was ordered.

On May 29, 2026, Austin Imaging documented on cervical MRI a C5-C6 disc protrusion with mild right foraminal narrowing, and stated that the findings may represent degenerative change and to correlate clinically.
On June 12, 2026, Hill Country Pain Management recommended a cervical epidural steroid injection and documented that the patient states symptoms began after the January collision.
